title: Unit Test: Microorganisms – Friend and Foe
subject: Science
instructions: Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks.

questions.q: Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
The nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in the root nodules of leguminous plants is:
Salt helps preserve food because it:
options: draws out water, so microorganisms cannot grow
questions.answer: (a) draws out water, so microorganisms cannot grow

questions.q: What are pathogens? Name one disease spread through contaminated water and one spread through air.
questions.answer: Pathogens are disease-causing microorganisms. Water: cholera or typhoid. Air: tuberculosis or the common cold.

questions.q: How does Lactobacillus change milk into curd?
questions.answer: Lactobacillus multiplies in milk and converts the milk sugar into lactic acid. This sets the milk into curd.

questions.q: What is fermentation? Who discovered it?
questions.answer: Fermentation is the conversion of sugar into alcohol by yeast. It was discovered by Louis Pasteur in 1857.

questions.q: How can microorganisms cause food poisoning? Give one way to prevent it.
questions.answer: Some microorganisms grow on food and produce toxic (poisonous) substances, so eating the spoilt food makes us sick. Prevention (any one): refrigerate food, cook it properly, cover it, eat it fresh.

questions.q: Name the type of microorganism (bacterium or virus) that causes:

subparts.q: foot and mouth disease in cattle

questions.q: How does a vaccine protect us from a disease? Who discovered the vaccine for smallpox?
questions.answer: A vaccine contains dead or weakened microbes. The body makes antibodies to fight them and remembers how to make them, so if the real disease-causing microbe enters later, it is destroyed quickly. Edward Jenner discovered the smallpox vaccine in 1798.

subparts.q: Explain how microorganisms are useful in (i) cleaning the environment, (ii) agriculture, (iii) medicine.
subparts.answer: (i) Decomposers break down dead plants, animals and organic waste into simple substances, keeping the environment clean. (ii) Bacteria such as Rhizobium, and blue-green algae, fix nitrogen and increase soil fertility. (iii) Antibiotics (e.g. penicillin) and vaccines are made from microorganisms.

subparts.q: Why should we not let water collect around our homes?
subparts.answer: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water. Mosquitoes spread diseases such as malaria (and dengue), so removing standing water stops them from breeding.
